name: Chancay Port
value: $1.3bn first phase; COSCO bought 60% of Terminales Portuarios Chancay for $225m in 2019
china_gets: Majority control of a deep-water Pacific hub with 1m TEU capacity and direct Shanghai routes; the terminal owns its land, so no concession is needed
host_position: Peru says Chancay will make it a regional trade hub and cut shipping time to China by 12 days; US officials have raised possible military use
confidence_reason: Stake and price in COSCO's own exchange filing; cost and inauguration confirmed by Peru's state news agency and Reuters

name: Espacio Lejano deep-space station (Neuquén)
value: 200-hectare site on a 50-year tax-free lease; China funded about $54.5m of construction (House Select Committee figure)
lender_builder: China Satellite Launch and Tracking Control General (CLTC, PLA-linked); China Harbour Engineering built it
china_gets: A 35m deep-space antenna in the southern hemisphere for tracking, command and data, run under Chinese labour law with no effective Argentine inspection
host_position: Argentina says the station is civilian (a 2016 addendum says so) and compares it to the ESA station in Mendoza
confidence_reason: The lease and PLA-linked operator are well documented; military use is alleged, not proven

name: Coca Codo Sinclair hydroelectric plant
value: $1.98bn EPC contract; $1.68bn China Exim loan at 6.9% (85% of cost); Ecuador's comptroller found 7,648 cracks
lender_builder: China Exim Bank; Sinohydro (PowerChina) built it
china_gets: The building contract, a 6.9% fixed-rate loan insured by Sinosure; in the 2025 settlement PowerChina takes over operation
host_position: Ecuador's largest power plant (1,500 MW); Ecuador went to ICC arbitration over defects, then in 2025 agreed to drop it
confidence_reason: Loan terms from AidData's project record; defects from Ecuador's Contraloría; settlement reported by Reuters

name: CDB oil-backed loans and PetroChina prepayments
value: Several CDB facilities, e.g. $2.05bn (2011, repaid early in 2018) and $2.03bn (2016); PetroChina $1bn oil prepayment
china_gets: Repayment from Petroecuador oil sales routed into CDB-controlled accounts with minimum balances; long-term crude supply
host_position: Ecuador says the loans financed infrastructure and has prepaid or rescheduled them, with maturities extended to 2027
confidence_reason: Loan facilities and repayment mechanics documented in AidData project records

name: Joint China-Venezuela Fund (oil-for-loans)
value: $60bn+ CDB commitments via the Joint Fund since 2007; AidData counts $105.6bn of Chinese loan commitments 2000-2018; $10-15bn estimated outstanding (2026)
lender_builder: China Development Bank; CNPC/ChinaOil buys the oil
china_gets: Oil cargoes for debt service, paid into a CDB collection account with set-off rights
host_position: Venezuela defaulted in 2017; China granted grace periods; US control of exports in 2026 caught cargoes that had been servicing Chinese debt
confidence_reason: Structure and totals from AidData; current outstanding range from Reuters citing SocGen and JPMorgan (estimates differ)

name: Uyuni lithium plants (YLB-CBC)
value: $1.03bn contract for two direct-extraction plants, 35,000 t/yr lithium carbonate
lender_builder: Hong Kong CBC consortium (includes CATL); state YLB holds 51%
china_gets: Building and operating rights at the world's largest lithium resource, at CBC's own cost and risk
host_position: Bolivia's government backs the deal; a court suspended its passage in 2025 pending environmental studies and indigenous consultation
confidence_reason: Contract signed and reported by Reuters and Bolivia's energy ministry, but not ratified and no plant is operating

name: Tianqi stake in SQM (Salar de Atacama)
value: About 22% of SQM held by Tianqi Lithium
china_gets: A large minority stake in the world's second-biggest lithium producer and a share of its Atacama brine output
host_position: Chile put Atacama lithium under a Codelco-SQM partnership; Tianqi's legal challenge was rejected by the Supreme Court in January 2026
confidence_reason: Stake and the court ruling reported by Chile's state defence council and Caixin

name: Cauchari-Olaroz lithium
value: 40,000 t/yr lithium carbonate; production began June 2023
lender_builder: Ganfeng Lithium (with Lithium Argentina and Jujuy's JEMSE)
china_gets: Lithium carbonate supply for Chinese battery makers
host_position: Jujuy province is a partner through JEMSE and backs lithium output as a source of revenue
confidence_reason: Start-up reported by market and Chinese business press; ownership shares not set out in these sources

name: Mariana lithium
value: 20,000 t/yr lithium chloride first phase; production began February 2025
china_gets: Lithium chloride feedstock for Ganfeng's refineries
host_position: Salta province promotes the project as investment and jobs
confidence_reason: Start-up in Ganfeng's exchange filing and Reuters; no investment figure in these sources

name: Tres Quebradas (3Q) lithium
value: 20,000 t/yr lithium carbonate first phase; production began September 2025
host_position: Catamarca province backs the project as investment
confidence_reason: Start-up reported only by the company; site could not be reached for verification

name: Néstor Kirchner and Jorge Cepernic dams (Santa Cruz)
value: $4.71bn syndicated loan (CDB $2.49bn, ICBC, Bank of China), signed 2014; works largely stalled since 2023
lender_builder: China Development Bank, ICBC, Bank of China; Gezhouba-led consortium builds
china_gets: The building contract and loan repayment; the deal was tied to the wider China-Argentina strategic partnership
host_position: Argentina says the 1,310 MW dams are needed for power; successive governments renegotiated and delayed them
confidence_reason: Loan in AidData's record and Argentina's Boletín Oficial; stalled status from Argentine press

name: Belgrano Cargas freight railway rehabilitation
value: $2.47bn CMEC contract (2010); $2.1bn CDB/ICBC buyer's credit (2012) covering 85%
lender_builder: China Development Bank, ICBC; China Machinery Engineering Corp (CMEC)
china_gets: The rehabilitation contract, Chinese rolling stock and rail supplies, and a freight route for northern grain to the ports
host_position: Argentina says the line cuts the cost of moving grain from the north to the river ports
confidence_reason: Contract and loan documented in AidData and Argentina's official contract text

name: China-Argentina currency swap
value: $18bn swap line; the activated CNY35bn (about $5bn) tranche was renewed in April 2025
china_gets: Wider use of the yuan in Argentina's reserves and trade and political leverage over a reserve-poor central bank
host_position: Argentina's central bank says the swap supports its reserves; the US has urged Argentina to end it

name: TCP container terminal, Paranaguá
value: R$2.9bn (about $924m) for 90% of TCP; deal closed February 2018
china_gets: Control of Brazil's third-largest container terminal, a main outlet for grain and meat exports
host_position: Brazil's transport ministry welcomed the investment
confidence_reason: Price and stake in CMPort's exchange filing and Brazil's transport ministry

name: State Grid Brazil: Belo Monte lines and CPFL Energia
value: Two ±800 kV Belo Monte UHV lines (won 2014 and 2015); 54.6% of CPFL Energia bought in 2017, later about 84%
lender_builder: State Grid Corporation of China (State Grid Brazil Holding)
china_gets: Ownership of long-distance transmission and Brazil's largest private distributor; a showcase for Chinese UHV technology
host_position: Brazil awarded the lines at public auction and approved the CPFL purchase
confidence_reason: Auctions from Brazil's mines and energy ministry; history from State Grid Brazil

name: CNOOC stake in the Stabroek Block
value: 25% working interest (ExxonMobil 45% operator; Hess/Chevron 30%); the block passed 500m barrels produced in 2024
china_gets: A quarter of the consortium's oil from one of the world's fastest-growing fields
host_position: Guyana says its share of the oil is rising as cost recovery falls
confidence_reason: Ownership shares widely reported, including by Guyana's own information department

name: Bogotá Metro Line 1
value: COP13.83 trillion concession (about $3.55bn, Reuters); 23.96km elevated line, 16 stations
lender_builder: China Harbour Engineering (85%) and Xi'an Rail Transportation Group (15%) as Metro Línea 1
china_gets: A 28-year concession to build, supply trains for and run the line for 20 years
host_position: Colombia's government and Bogotá signed it as the city's first metro
confidence_reason: Concession terms from Colombia's transport ministry and Bogotá city hall

name: Mirador copper mine
value: $329m CDB-backed loan to buy Corriente Resources (2010); $1.29bn syndicated loan for mine development (2014); exports began 2019
lender_builder: CRCC-Tongguan (China Railway Construction Corp and Tongling Nonferrous) via EcuaCorriente; China Development Bank
china_gets: Ecuador's first large-scale copper mine and its concentrate
host_position: Ecuador's government signed an addendum to expand output; local and indigenous groups contest its impact
confidence_reason: Loans in AidData records; first exports reported by Reuters

name: Las Bambas copper mine
value: $5.85bn purchase from Glencore (2014) by an MMG-led Chinese consortium; MMG announced a $2bn investment in 2022
china_gets: One of the world's biggest copper mines and its concentrate
host_position: Peru counts on the mine for revenue; communities have blocked the mining road repeatedly over land and compensation
confidence_reason: Price from CITIC; conflicts and investment reported by Reuters
